note: Adapted from Ahmad's (1965) description of the new species, originally in English; the original describes the king (dealated alate) and the soldier and does not describe the worker; table 18 lists only the measurements of the king (morphotype), some of them incomplete in the original typesetting, so only the items that could be read with certainty are entered; figure 52 (alate head and pronotum, head in profile, antenna) and figure 53 (the same for the soldier, with the mandibles and postmentum) are not translated.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head dark brown; postclypeus brown; labrum with a brown transverse band in the middle; antennae brown; pronotum dark brown, the disc with a T-shaped pale brown mark, each anterolateral corner and the middle of the posterior margin with an eye-spot-like mark. Head densely hairy; postclypeus as densely hairy as the head; middle of the labrum with short fine hairs; pronotum densely hairy. Head semicircular; fontanelle distinct, broadly oval, situated below the level of the ocelli (eye spots). Eyes large and bulging, nearly circular, their distance from the lower margin of the head 1/5 of their short diameter. Ocelli large, broadly oval, less than their short diameter from the eyes. Postclypeus inflated, about half as long as wide. Labrum dome-shaped, the apex membranous. Antennae incomplete (the antennae of the specimen are broken); segment 2 1.5 times as long as segment 3, segment 4 nearly as long as segment 3. Pronotum narrower than the head, about half as long as wide; anterior margin nearly straight, with an indistinct median notch; posterior margin slightly concave. Measurements of the king (dealate): head length (to the lateral base of the mandibles) 1.58 mm, head width 2.30 mm, long diameter of the eye 0.67 mm, short diameter of the eye 0.54 mm, distance from the lower margin of the eye 0.10 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head smoky brown, slightly paler in front; labrum brown; mandibles dark brown; antennae brown, the basal segments paler. Head with very sparse hairs; labrum with a row of long setae along its margin; anterior margin of the postmentum with 2 short setae; pronotum sparsely hairy. Head oval; lateral margins convex, widest in the middle. Labrum with parallel lateral margins, broadly rounded in front. Mandibles half as long as the head capsule; left mandible with 3 notches at the base; right mandible more curved than the left, with fine serrations near the molar plate. Postmentum 1.5 times as long as wide, the sides convex, widest in the middle. Antennae 16-segmented; segment 2 1.5 times as long as segment 3 and 2 times as long as segment 4; segment 4 shortest. Anterior part of the pronotum slightly concave, posterior margin broad and shallowly concave; lateral lobes broadly rounded. Measurements of 13 soldiers (holotype/range/mean): head length (to the lateral base of the mandibles) 1.22/1.14—1.40/1.26 mm, head width (at the base of the mandibles) 0.70/0.62—0.88/0.69 mm, head width at the posterior lateral corners of the antennal carinae 0.93/0.806—1.01/0.92 mm, maximum head width 1.11/0.98—1.19/1.08 mm, left mandible length 0.65/0.52—0.65/0.58 mm, postmentum length 0.78/0.65—0.83/0.74 mm, postmentum width 0.52/0.44—0.57/0.48 mm, pronotum length 0.44/0.39—0.52/0.43 mm, pronotum width 0.75/0.65—0.83/0.72 mm.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is very close to Hypotermes obscuriceps but is distinctly darker; in winifredae the ocelli are closer to the eyes and in xenotermitis they are smaller. The soldier is very close to xenotermitis, from which it differs in the more strongly curved right mandible, the darker colour and the non-parallel sides of the postmentum; the soldier of obscuriceps has a less constricted head with straighter lateral margins; the soldier of winifredae is larger with a nearly square head; the soldier of sumatrensis is smaller with parallel sides of the head.
